chunk_map.heading: A file it reads every time

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L8: "That's a guardrail. That's your turn." Closest to violating: "That" binds to the file-read-every-session idea in L6, the immediately preceding sentence; "guardrail" is the slide's own predicate noun, not a referent. Harm (reader cannot resolve a pointer) absent.

No cross-file or positional callback in L4-L8; L4 "So far" is a within-deck sequential reference to the single typed message, which the deck (context-is-king) has shown. Harm (callback aims at wrong file) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4 "the context was one message you typed" describes the typed-prompt beat taught on the preceding slides, not a named did/saw/caught beat; no "the X you did" construction. Harm (dead beat reference) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess/reveal demo beat on this slide

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-L8: slide carries a self-contained claim (context can live in a file read every session; you write it once). Closest: L8 "That's a guardrail. That's your turn." is a kicker, but L6 carries the claim.
Header "A file it reads every time" (L1) vs L6 "a file the agent reads at the start of every session": header literally true; "it" = the agent, resolved by L6.

L8 "That's a guardrail. That's your turn." is a two-beat pair, not Not-X-Not-Y-Z, not a triple, no superlative, no number, no noun stack, no verb triplet. Grep: em_dash 0, banned_words 0 (CLEAN per view).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep banned/dialect terms (compendium, forcing function, beat, surface-as-noun, mood) in body L1-L9 -> none; "guardrail" is ordinary engineering vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c "\*\*" in body L1-L9 -> 0 bold elements; budget <=1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: slide file included by lectures; presence in composed deck is guarded by include mechanism and slides.test.js, no phase-less section here

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/a-file-it-reads-every-time.md -> "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/slides/a-file-it-reads-every-time.md -> "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no links in body; has_urls false, no in-body links

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/a-file-it-reads-every-time.md -> "oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits"; slide has 0 bullets, ~60 words.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: lecture-slide header; rule scopes law/consolidation claim headers and exercise grammar; header "A file it reads every time" is a catalogue/orientation entry naming its subject, not an exercise heading

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L8 "That's a guardrail. That's your turn." is the closest to a (c) aphorism kicker, but it names the guardrail frame and hands the turn, adding a move the slide does not otherwise hold (L6 states the mechanism, not the classification); not a restatement of the header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git diff b58bcc4c..HEAD shows body rewrite under unchanged header L1 "A file it reads every time"; no header change, no inherited stale bullets (L4-L6 answer the header).

notes: Single-slide file; accept-note found: Quality line only (no dated decision notes). Rule 10 N/A because include mechanism guards presence. "guardrail"/"your turn" are not defined earlier in context-is-king but resolve on the slide (predicate noun); shared with claude-basics deck where guardrail is module vocabulary.
